```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

set.seed(260521)

library(tidyverse)
library(smoothbp)
library(brms)       # group-membership logistic model only
library(gt)
options(smoothbp.cores = parallel::detectCores())

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Version guard. smoothbp 0.2.8 fixes a NUTS proposal-rule error in the
# random-effects sampler that affects every random-intercept fit produced by
# 0.2.x, so a render against an earlier build is invalid rather than merely
# out of date.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
.MIN_SMOOTHBP <- "0.2.8"
if (utils::packageVersion("smoothbp") < .MIN_SMOOTHBP) {
  stop(sprintf(
    paste0("smoothbp %s is loaded from\n  %s\nbut >= %s is required.\n",
           ".libPaths()[1] = %s\n",
           "Install smoothbp >= %s into this project's library,\n",
           "then restart R and re-knit."),
    utils::packageVersion("smoothbp"),
    dirname(system.file(package = "smoothbp")),
    .MIN_SMOOTHBP, .libPaths()[1], .MIN_SMOOTHBP))
}
```

```{r supplement-registry, include = FALSE}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Single source of truth for supplementary numbering. Headings, table titles
# and in-text cross-references all read from here, so re-ordering the
# supplement means editing these three vectors and nothing else.
# See supplementary_label_map.md for the mapping to the previous S-numbering.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
NOTE <- c(exclusions   = 1, selection  = 2, coefficients = 3, diagnostics = 4,
          sharpness    = 5, transition = 6, subtests     = 7, attrition   = 8,
          sbc          = 9, ppc        = 10)

TAB  <- c(exclusions   = 1, selection    = 2, coefficients  = 3,
          convergence  = 4, loo          = 5, rho_grid      = 6,
          er_resolution = 7, omega_bounds = 8, omega_group  = 9,
          subtests     = 10, waves       = 11, baseline_attrition = 12,
          attrition_refit = 13)

FIG  <- c(ppc = 1)

sn <- function(k) sprintf("Supplementary Note %d",  NOTE[[k]])
st <- function(k) sprintf("Supplementary Table %d", TAB[[k]])
sf <- function(k) sprintf("Supplementary Fig. %d",  FIG[[k]])

# Display labels
DOMAINS <- c(episodic  = "Episodic memory",    working  = "Working memory",
             executive = "Executive function", language = "Language processing")
```

```{r data-prep, include = FALSE}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SYNTHETIC DATA. The study data cannot be shared, so this supplement reads the
# synthetic release in data/synthetic/ (made by thbp_synthesise_all_domains.R).
# Every number it produces will differ from the submitted supplement.
#
# The synthetic files hold the composite domain scores directly (one row per
# participant-wave, executive function already sign-reversed so higher is
# better, covariates already standardised), so the sub-test z-scoring and
# compositing that was here is replaced by the lines below (the method is in the
# manuscript Methods). The objects built here have the
# same names and columns as before, so nothing downstream is changed.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
read_domain <- function(file)
  read.csv(file.path('data/synthetic', file)) |> mutate(IDCode = factor(IDCode))

episodic  <- read_domain('epis.csv')
working   <- read_domain('wm.csv')
executive <- read_domain('ef.csv')
language  <- read_domain('lang.csv')

# d3: one row per participant-wave with the four composites side by side, as
# before (executive un-flipped, as it was here before the flip). Waves are
# matched across domains on years since baseline, and on order within a year
# when two assessments fall in the same year.
waves <- bind_rows(episodic = episodic, working = working,
                   executive = executive, language = language, .id = 'name') |>
  group_by(name, IDCode, years_since_baseline) |>
  mutate(k = row_number()) |>
  ungroup()

d3 <- waves |>
  select(IDCode, Group, years_since_baseline, k, name, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = name, values_from = value) |>
  arrange(IDCode, years_since_baseline, k) |>
  group_by(IDCode) |>
  mutate(phase = row_number()) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(executive = -executive)

# demographics: one row per participant; Sessions = assessment waves completed
demographics <- waves |>
  distinct(IDCode, Group, Sex, Age_t1, education_total, wtar_fsiq_baseline,
           drs_tot_raw_baseline, hads_anx_baseline, hads_dep_baseline) |>
  left_join(count(d3, IDCode, name = 'Sessions'), by = 'IDCode')
```

```{r posterior-helpers, include = FALSE}
# Draws as a plain data.frame, dropping posterior's .chain/.iteration/.draw columns
.draws <- function(m) {
  d <- as.data.frame(posterior::as_draws_df(m$draws))
  d[, !grepl("^\\.", names(d)), drop = FALSE]
}

# Posterior draws of a parameter or of a sum of parameters
.combo <- function(m, vars) {
  d <- .draws(m)
  miss <- setdiff(vars, names(d))
  if (length(miss)) stop("Parameter(s) not found in draws: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "))
  if (length(vars) == 1L) d[[vars]] else rowSums(d[, vars, drop = FALSE])
}

post <- function(m, vars, probs = c(.025, .975)) {
  x <- .combo(m, vars)
  c(mean = mean(x),
    lo   = unname(quantile(x, probs[1])),
    hi   = unname(quantile(x, probs[2])))
}

ci  <- function(v, digits = 2)
  sprintf("%.*f [%.*f, %.*f]", digits, v[["mean"]], digits, v[["lo"]], digits, v[["hi"]])
pci <- function(m, vars, digits = 2) ci(post(m, vars), digits)
pH  <- function(m, vars) mean(.combo(m, vars) > 0)

er_of  <- function(p) if (p >= 1) Inf else p / (1 - p)
fmt_er <- function(p, digits = 1) {
  er <- er_of(p)
  if (!is.finite(er) || er > 1000) "> 1000" else formatC(er, format = "f", digits = digits)
}
fmt_p <- function(p, digits = 3) formatC(p, format = "f", digits = digits)

# Frequentist p-values for display: "< 0.001" rather than "0.000"
fmt_pval <- function(p, digits = 3)
  ifelse(p < 10^-digits, paste0("< ", formatC(10^-digits, format = "f", digits = digits)),
         formatC(p, format = "f", digits = digits))

n_against <- function(m, vars) sum(.combo(m, vars) <= 0)

conv <- function(m) {
  s <- posterior::summarise_draws(m$draws, "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail")
  s <- s[!is.na(s$rhat), ]
  list(max_rhat = max(s$rhat), min_bulk = min(s$ess_bulk), min_tail = min(s$ess_tail),
       n_div = m$n_divergent)
}

GB1 <- "b1_GroupExperimental"
GD1 <- "delta1_GroupExperimental"
```

```{r table-style, include = FALSE}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# House style for supplementary tables. `key` indexes TAB, so the table
# number in the title always agrees with the registry.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
supp_gt <- function(data, key, title, subtitle = NULL, pdf_font = 11, ...) {
  pdf <- knitr::is_latex_output()
  tbl <- gt::gt(data, id = paste0("tab-", gsub("_", "-", key)), ...) |>
    gt::tab_header(
      title    = gt::md(sprintf("**%s.** %s", st(key), title)),
      subtitle = if (is.null(subtitle)) NULL else gt::md(subtitle)
    ) |>
    gt::opt_align_table_header(align = "left") |>
    gt::tab_options(
      table.width                       = gt::pct(100),
      table.font.size                   = gt::px(14),
      heading.title.font.size           = gt::px(16),
      heading.subtitle.font.size        = gt::px(13.5),
      heading.padding                   = gt::px(4),
      heading.border.bottom.color       = "#333333",
      heading.border.bottom.width       = gt::px(2),
      table.border.top.style            = "hidden",
      column_labels.font.weight         = "bold",
      column_labels.background.color    = "#f4f6f8",
      column_labels.border.bottom.color = "#333333",
      column_labels.border.bottom.width = gt::px(1),
      row_group.font.weight             = "bold",
      row_group.background.color        = "#fafafa",
      row_group.border.top.color        = "#bbbbbb",
      table_body.border.bottom.color    = "#333333",
      table_body.border.bottom.width    = gt::px(2),
      data_row.padding                  = gt::px(5),
      footnotes.font.size               = gt::px(12.5),
      source_notes.font.size            = gt::px(12.5)
    )
  if (pdf) {
    # PDF: shrink to fit the text block, and pin each table where it is written
    # instead of letting it float ([t] by default), which detached tables from
    # their notes. latex.tbl.pos needs gt >= 0.11.
    tbl <- gt::tab_options(tbl, table.font.size = gt::px(pdf_font))
    if ("latex.tbl.pos" %in% names(formals(gt::tab_options)))
      tbl <- gt::tab_options(tbl, latex.tbl.pos = "H")
    else
      warning("gt < 0.11: tables will float in the PDF; update gt to pin them in place.")
  }
  tbl
}

# Raw variable/term-name columns are kept in the HTML but dropped from the PDF,
# where they push wide tables off the page.
pdf_hide <- function(tbl, columns)
  if (knitr::is_latex_output()) gt::cols_hide(tbl, {{ columns }}) else tbl

# Column labels and spanners with Greek/maths. gt passes html() content through
# verbatim in both formats, so give each format its own markup: HTML entities for
# the HTML output, LaTeX maths (with % escaped) for the PDF.
lab <- function(html, latex) gt::html(if (knitr::is_latex_output()) latex else html)

# Monospace for raw variable / term names
mono <- function(tbl, columns)
  gt::tab_style(tbl, gt::cell_text(font = "monospace", size = gt::px(12.5), color = "#555"),
                gt::cells_body(columns = {{ columns }}))
```

```{r model-priors, include = FALSE}
THBP_PRIORS <- smoothbp_priors(
  b0      = prior_normal(0, 2),
  b1      = prior_normal(0, 2),
  deltas  = prior_normal(0, 1),
  omega   = list(list("(Intercept)" = prior_normal(3, 2, lb = 1, ub = 6))),
  rho     = prior_normal(2, 2, lb = 1),   # not used: rho is fixed below
  sigma   = prior_invgamma(shape = 2, scale = 1),
  sigma_u = prior_invgamma(shape = 2, scale = 1)
)

fit_domain <- function(dat, seed = 42L) {
  smoothbp(
    formula = value ~ years_since_baseline,
    b0      = ~ 1 + Group + education_total_s + Age_t1_s + Sex +
                hads_anx_baseline + hads_dep_baseline +
                wtar_fsiq_baseline_s + drs_tot_raw_baseline_s +
                (1 | IDCode),
    b1      = ~ 1 + Group,
    deltas  = list(~ 1 + Group),
    omega   = list(~ 1),
    rho     = list(fixed(3)),
    data    = dat,
    priors  = THBP_PRIORS,
    chains  = 4L, iter = 10000L, warmup = 5000L,
    target_accept = 0.99, seed = seed
  )
}
```

```{r fit-episodic, include = FALSE}
m.ep <- fit_domain(episodic)
```

```{r fit-selection, include = FALSE}
m.group <- brm(
  bf(Group ~ scale(education_total) +
               scale(Age_t1) +
               Sex +
               hads_anx_baseline +
               hads_dep_baseline +
               scale(wtar_fsiq_baseline) +
               scale(drs_tot_raw_baseline)),
  family = bernoulli(),
  data   = demographics
)
```

```{r fit-completion, include = FALSE}
add_sessions <- function(dat) {
  dat |>
    left_join(demographics |> select(IDCode, Sessions), by = 'IDCode') |>
    mutate(Sessions_s = as.numeric(scale(Sessions))) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Sessions_s))
}

episodic_s <- add_sessions(episodic)
language_s <- add_sessions(language)

fit_sessions <- function(dat, seed = 42L) {
  smoothbp(
    formula = value ~ years_since_baseline,
    b0      = ~ 1 + Group + Sessions_s + education_total_s + Age_t1_s + Sex +
                hads_anx_baseline + hads_dep_baseline +
                wtar_fsiq_baseline_s + drs_tot_raw_baseline_s +
                (1 | IDCode),
    b1      = ~ 1 + Group + Sessions_s,
    deltas  = list(~ 1 + Group),
    omega   = list(~ 1),
    rho     = list(fixed(3)),
    data    = dat,
    priors  = THBP_PRIORS,
    chains  = 4L, iter = 10000L, warmup = 5000L,
    target_accept = 0.99, seed = seed
  )
}

m.ep.s <- fit_sessions(episodic_s)
m.la.s <- fit_sessions(language_s)
```

```{r tab-exclusions}

  Domain       = unname(DOMAINS),

) |>

## `r sn("selection")` — Predictors of group membership {#note-selection}

```{r tab-selection}
fe <- brms::fixef(m.group)
hy <- brms::hypothesis(m.group, c(
  'scaleeducation_total > 0',
  'scaleAge_t1 < 0',
  'SexMale < 0',
  'hads_anx_baseline > 0',
  'hads_dep_baseline < 0',
  'scalewtar_fsiq_baseline > 0',
  'scaledrs_tot_raw_baseline > 0'
))$hypothesis

r2_bayes <- brms::bayes_R2(m.group)[1, "Estimate"]
n_group  <- stats::nobs(m.group)

sel_terms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~term,                        ~label,                                 ~dir,
  "Intercept",                  "Intercept",                            NA,
  "scaleeducation_total",       "Education (years, standardised)",      "> 0",
  "scaleAge_t1",                "Age at baseline (standardised)",       "< 0",
  "SexMale",                    "Sex: male",                            "< 0",
  "hads_anx_baseline",          "HADS anxiety, baseline",               "> 0",
  "hads_dep_baseline",          "HADS depression, baseline",            "< 0",
  "scalewtar_fsiq_baseline",    "WTAR premorbid IQ (standardised)",     "> 0",
  "scaledrs_tot_raw_baseline",  "DRS total, baseline (standardised)",   "> 0"
)

sel_tbl <- sel_terms |>
  mutate(
    or    = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", exp(fe[term, "Estimate"]),
                    exp(fe[term, "Q2.5"]), exp(fe[term, "Q97.5"])),
    h_est = c(NA, sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", hy$Estimate, hy$CI.Lower, hy$CI.Upper)),
    h_er  = c(NA, sprintf("%.2f", hy$Evid.Ratio)),
    h_pp  = c(NA, sprintf("%.2f", hy$Post.Prob))
  )

sel_tbl |>
  select(label, term, or, dir, h_est, h_er, h_pp) |>
  supp_gt("selection",
          "Bayesian logistic regression of group membership on baseline covariates",
          subtitle = sprintf(paste(
            "Outcome: Education group (vs Control); N = %d. Bayesian R² = %.3f:",
            "approximately %.0f%% of the variance in group membership is explained by",
            "these seven variables jointly."), n_group, r2_bayes, 100 * r2_bayes)) |>
  gt::cols_label(label = "Predictor", term = "Term", or = "Odds ratio [95% CrI]",
                 dir = "Direction", h_est = "Log-odds [90% CrI]",
                 h_er = "ER", h_pp = "P(H)") |>
  gt::tab_spanner("Directional hypothesis", columns = c(dir, h_est, h_er, h_pp)) |>
  gt::sub_missing(missing_text = "—") |>
  gt::cols_align("left",  columns = c(label, term)) |>
  gt::cols_align("right", columns = c(or, dir, h_est, h_er, h_pp)) |>
  mono(term) |>
  pdf_hide(term) |>
  gt::tab_footnote(
    "One-sided hypotheses: credible intervals are 90%. ER = evidence ratio, P(H)/(1 − P(H)).",
    locations = gt::cells_column_spanners("Directional hypothesis"))
```

## `r sn("coefficients")` — Full posterior summaries of the trajectory models {#note-coefficients}

Throughout, `Group` is coded `Control`/`Experimental` in the raw data and this level name
appears wherever model output is printed directly (e.g. `GroupExperimental`). In the main
text, figures and Table 1 the same arm is called "Education".

```{r tab-coefficients}
COEF_ROWS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~block,                                        ~term,                        ~label,
  "β₀ — Intercept and covariates",    "b0_(Intercept)",             "Intercept",
  "β₀ — Intercept and covariates",    "b0_GroupExperimental",       "Group: Education",
  "β₀ — Intercept and covariates",    "b0_education_total_s",       "Education (years, standardised)",
  "β₀ — Intercept and covariates",    "b0_Age_t1_s",                "Age at baseline (standardised)",
  "β₀ — Intercept and covariates",    "b0_SexMale",                 "Sex: male",
  "β₀ — Intercept and covariates",    "b0_hads_anx_baseline",       "HADS anxiety, baseline",
  "β₀ — Intercept and covariates",    "b0_hads_dep_baseline",       "HADS depression, baseline",
  "β₀ — Intercept and covariates",    "b0_wtar_fsiq_baseline_s",    "WTAR premorbid IQ (standardised)",
  "β₀ — Intercept and covariates",    "b0_drs_tot_raw_baseline_s",  "DRS total, baseline (standardised)",
  "β₁ — Pre-transition slope",        "b1_(Intercept)",             "Intercept",
  "β₁ — Pre-transition slope",        "b1_GroupExperimental",       "Group: Education",
  "δ₁ — Slope change at transition",  "delta1_(Intercept)",         "Intercept",
  "δ₁ — Slope change at transition",  "delta1_GroupExperimental",   "Group: Education",
  "ω₁ — Transition point (years)",    "omega1_(Intercept)",         "Intercept",
  "ρ₁ — Transition sharpness",        "rho1_(Intercept)",           "Intercept",
  "Variance components",                         "sigma",                      "σ, residual SD",
  "Variance components",                         "sigma_u",                    "σᵤ, random-intercept SD"
)

coef_cell <- function(d, term) {
  if (!term %in% names(d)) {
    # random-intercept SD may carry a grouping suffix (e.g. sigma_u_IDCode)
    hit <- grep(paste0("^", term), names(d), value = TRUE)
    if (!length(hit)) return(NA_character_)
    term <- hit[1]
  }
  x <- d[[term]]
  if (sd(x) == 0) return(sprintf("%.2f (fixed)", x[1]))
  sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", mean(x), quantile(x, .025), quantile(x, .975))
}

coef_tbl <- COEF_ROWS
for (k in names(DOMAINS)) {
  d <- .draws(MODELS[[DOMAINS[[k]]]])
  coef_tbl[[k]] <- vapply(COEF_ROWS$term, coef_cell, character(1), d = d)
}

coef_tbl |>
  supp_gt("coefficients",
          "Posterior summaries for all trajectory-model parameters, by cognitive domain",
          subtitle = "Posterior mean [95% credible interval]. Slopes are z per year.",
          groupname_col = "block", pdf_font = 10) |>
  gt::cols_label(label = "Parameter", term = "Term",
                 episodic = DOMAINS[["episodic"]], working  = DOMAINS[["working"]],
                 executive = DOMAINS[["executive"]], language = DOMAINS[["language"]]) |>
  gt::sub_missing(missing_text = "—") |>
  gt::cols_align("left",  columns = c(label, term)) |>
  gt::cols_align("right", columns = all_of(names(DOMAINS))) |>
  mono(term) |>
  pdf_hide(term)
```

## `r sn("diagnostics")` — Convergence and cross-validation diagnostics {#note-diagnostics}

```{r tab-convergence}
tibble(Domain = names(MODELS)) |>
  bind_cols(bind_rows(lapply(MODELS, function(m) as_tibble(conv(m))))) |>
  supp_gt("convergence", "MCMC convergence diagnostics by domain",
          subtitle = "4 chains × 5,000 post-warmup iterations (20,000 draws) per model.") |>
  gt::cols_label(max_rhat = lab("Max R&#770;", "Max $\\hat{R}$"), min_bulk = "Min bulk ESS",
                 min_tail = "Min tail ESS", n_div = "Divergent transitions") |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = max_rhat, decimals = 3) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(min_bulk, min_tail), decimals = 0) |>
  gt::cols_align("left", columns = Domain)
```

Full per-domain reports, including the fitted model with posterior means substituted and
asymptotic pre- and post-transition slopes`r if (knitr::is_html_output()) " (select a domain to expand)"`:

```{r model-reports, results = 'asis'}
for (nm in names(MODELS)) {
  out <- utils::capture.output(model_results(MODELS[[nm]]))
  if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
    cat("\n```{=html}\n",
        '<details class="model-report"><summary>', htmltools::htmlEscape(nm),
        " — full model report</summary>\n<pre>",
        htmltools::htmlEscape(paste(out, collapse = "\n")),
        "</pre></details>\n```\n\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    # PDF: each report as a plain verbatim block under a bold domain label
    cat("\n**", nm, "**\n\n```\n", paste(out, collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n\n", sep = "")
  }
}
```

Leave-one-out cross-validation is reported here as a diagnostic rather than as a model
comparison. It is used only as a secondary check on structural specification and not to
select among reported effect estimates, because its importance-sampling approximation is
not fully reliable for this model class: Pareto-$\hat{k}$ exceeds 0.7 for a small number of
observations in every domain and exceeds 1 in executive function and language processing.

```{r tab-loo}
loo_list <- lapply(MODELS, loo)

bind_rows(lapply(names(loo_list), function(nm) {
  l <- loo_list[[nm]]
  k <- tryCatch(loo::pareto_k_values(l), error = function(e) l$diagnostics$pareto_k)
  tibble(Domain = nm,
         n_obs  = length(k),
         elpd   = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", l$estimates["elpd_loo", "Estimate"],
                                         l$estimates["elpd_loo", "SE"]),
         p_loo  = l$estimates["p_loo", "Estimate"],
         k_hi   = sum(k > 0.7 & k <= 1),
         k_vhi  = sum(k > 1))
})) |>
  supp_gt("loo", "Leave-one-out cross-validation diagnostics",
          subtitle = "Reported as a diagnostic, not used for model selection.") |>
  gt::cols_label(n_obs = "Observations", elpd = "elpd_loo (SE)", p_loo = "p_loo",
                 k_hi = "(0.7, 1]", k_vhi = "> 1") |>
  gt::tab_spanner(lab("Observations with Pareto k&#770;", "Observations with Pareto $\\hat{k}$"), columns = c(k_hi, k_vhi)) |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = n_obs) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = p_loo, decimals = 1) |>
  gt::cols_align("left", columns = Domain) |>
  gt::cols_align("right", columns = elpd)
```

## `r sn("sharpness")` — Sensitivity to transition sharpness ($\rho$) {#note-sharpness}

All four domains were refitted at $\rho \in \{2, 3, 5\}$ and with $\rho$ estimated under
$N(2,2)$ truncated at 1 (`sensitivity_3.1_rho_grid.R`).

```{r tab-rho-grid, eval = file.exists("sensitivity_3.1_rho_grid_table.csv")}
read.csv('sensitivity_3.1_rho_grid_table.csv') |>
  transmute(Domain = unname(DOMAINS[domain]),
            rho    = as.character(rho_setting),
            omega  = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", omega_mean, omega_q5, omega_q95),
            d1grp  = sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]", delta1_grp_mean,
                             delta1_grp_q5, delta1_grp_q95),
            ph_b1  = sprintf("%.3f", PH_b1grp),
            ph_sum = sprintf("%.4f", PH_b1grp_d1grp),
            # From the evidence ratio, not from P(H): the stored P(H) is rounded
            # to four decimals, which cannot resolve three draws from four out
            # of 20,000. ER = (N - k) / k, so k = N / (ER + 1).
            against = round(20000 / (ER_b1grp_d1grp + 1))) |>
  supp_gt("rho_grid",
          "Sensitivity of the transition point and group contrasts to transition sharpness",
          subtitle = "Intervals are 90%. Conclusions are unchanged across settings.",
          groupname_col = "Domain") |>
  gt::cols_label(rho    = lab("&rho;", "$\\rho$"),
                 omega  = lab("&omega; [90% CrI]", "$\\omega$ [90\\% CrI]"),
                 d1grp  = lab("&delta;<sub>1</sub> group [90% CrI]", "$\\delta_1$ group [90\\% CrI]"),
                 ph_b1  = lab("&beta;<sub>1</sub> group", "$\\beta_1$ group"),
                 ph_sum = lab("&beta;<sub>1</sub> + &delta;<sub>1</sub> group", "$\\beta_1 + \\delta_1$ group"),
                 against = lab("Draws against &beta;<sub>1</sub> + &delta;<sub>1</sub>", "Draws against $\\beta_1 + \\delta_1$")) |>
  gt::tab_spanner("P(H)", columns = c(ph_b1, ph_sum)) |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = against) |>
  gt::cols_align("left", columns = rho) |>
  gt::cols_align("right", columns = c(omega, d1grp, ph_b1, ph_sum, against))
```

Posterior intervals for $\omega$ and $\delta_1$ are stable across settings, maximum $\hat{R}$ = 1.012, minimum bulk effective
sample size 541. The evidence ratio for the language post-transition contrast is less
stable: it takes values between roughly 5000 and 6700 across these fits, corresponding to
four or three draws out of 20,000 falling against the hypothesis. A ratio fixed by a
handful of draws reflects Monte Carlo variation in the extreme tail rather than sensitivity
of the finding, and is the basis for the reporting convention described
[below](#resolution-of-evidence-ratios).

### Resolution of evidence ratios {#resolution-of-evidence-ratios}

With 20,000 posterior draws, an evidence ratio of 1000 corresponds to 20 draws falling against the
hypothesis. The Monte Carlo standard error on
such counts is of the same order as the counts themselves, so the numerical value of a large
evidence ratio is not a stable summary of the evidence: across transition-sharpness settings
that leave the posterior interval essentially unchanged, the same contrast yields ratios of
roughly 5000 or 6700 depending on whether four draws or three fall against it.

We therefore cap reported evidence ratios at "> 1000" and interpret contrasts in that range
by their posterior intervals. Draw counts against each hypothesis:

```{r tab-er-resolution}
tibble(
  Domain  = names(MODELS),
  b1      = vapply(MODELS, n_against, numeric(1), vars = GB1),
  b1d1    = vapply(MODELS, n_against, numeric(1), vars = c(GB1, GD1))
) |>
  supp_gt("er_resolution", "Posterior draws falling against each directional hypothesis",
          subtitle = "Out of 20,000 posterior draws per model. Hypothesis: Education > Control.") |>
  gt::cols_label(b1   = lab("&beta;<sub>1</sub> group", "$\\beta_1$ group"),
                 b1d1 = lab("&beta;<sub>1</sub> + &delta;<sub>1</sub> group", "$\\beta_1 + \\delta_1$ group")) |>
  gt::tab_spanner("Draws against hypothesis", columns = c(b1, b1d1)) |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = c(b1, b1d1)) |>
  gt::cols_align("left", columns = Domain)
```

## `r sn("transition")` — Specification checks on the transition point {#note-transition}

### Sensitivity to the prior bounds {#omega-prior-bounds}

The $\omega$ prior truncates at 1 and 6 years. Three of four domains' credible intervals sit
close to the lower bound, so all four models were refitted with bounds widened to 0.5 and 8
(mean and SD unchanged; `sensitivity_3.2_omega_bounds.R`).

```{r tab-omega-bounds, eval = file.exists("sensitivity_3.2_omega_bounds_table.csv")}
read.csv('sensitivity_3.2_omega_bounds_table.csv') |>
  transmute(Domain   = unname(DOMAINS[domain]),
            headline = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", headline_mean, headline_lo, headline_hi),
            widened  = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", widened_mean, widened_lo, widened_hi),
            shift    = sprintf("%+.2f", shift)) |>
  supp_gt("omega_bounds", "Transition point under headline and widened prior bounds",
          subtitle = "Years since baseline. Both columns are 95% credible intervals.") |>
  gt::cols_label(headline = "Headline bounds (1, 6)",
                 widened  = "Widened bounds (0.5, 8)",
                 shift    = "Shift in mean") |>
  gt::tab_spanner(lab("&omega; [95% CrI]", "$\\omega$ [95\\% CrI]"), columns = c(headline, widened)) |>
  gt::cols_align("left", columns = Domain) |>
  gt::cols_align("right", columns = c(headline, widened, shift))
```

Episodic and working memory domains are robust to the truncation. Executive function and language
processing shift more, by 0.17 and 0.15 years, and their lower bounds track the new floor
rather than stabilising away from it, sitting 0.07 and 0.10 years above it. Executive
function's widened interval also reaches 6.01 years, past the upper bound of the headline
prior, so that interval was shaped by the truncation at both ends. We therefore describe
$\omega$ as data-identified in episodic memory, reasonably robust in working memory, and
substantially prior-informed in executive function and language processing — including in
the domain carrying the second supported finding.

### Transition point by group {#omega-by-group}

All four domains were refitted with $\omega \sim 1 + \text{Group}$, $\rho$ fixed at 3 and
everything else as in the primary specification (`sensitivity_2.3_omega_group.R`).

```{r tab-omega-group, eval = file.exists("sensitivity_2.3_omega_group_table.csv")}
read.csv('sensitivity_2.3_omega_group_table.csv') |>
  transmute(Domain    = unname(DOMAINS[domain]),
            grp       = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", omega_group_mean,
                                omega_group_lo90, omega_group_hi90),
            rhat      = omega_block_max_rhat,
            bulk      = omega_block_min_bulk,
            tail      = omega_block_min_tail,
            preferred = preferred_by_loo,
            elpd      = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", elpd_diff, se_diff)) |>
  supp_gt("omega_group", "Models allowing the transition point to differ by group",
          subtitle = paste("Group term in years since baseline, 90% credible interval.",
                           "Diagnostics are for the ω block; the elpd difference is the",
                           "group-varying model against the preferred one.")) |>
  gt::cols_label(grp       = "Group term [90% CrI]",
                 rhat      = lab("Max R&#770;", "Max $\\hat{R}$"),
                 bulk      = "Min bulk ESS",
                 tail      = "Min tail ESS",
                 preferred = "Preferred",
                 elpd      = "elpd difference (SE)") |>
  gt::tab_spanner(lab("&omega; block diagnostics", "$\\omega$ block diagnostics"), columns = c(rhat, bulk, tail)) |>
  gt::tab_spanner("Leave-one-out", columns = c(preferred, elpd)) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = rhat, decimals = 3) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(bulk, tail), decimals = 0) |>
  gt::cols_align("left", columns = Domain) |>
  gt::cols_align("right", columns = c(grp, elpd)) |>
  gt::cols_align("center", columns = preferred) |>
  mono(preferred)
```

The group term was well identified in every domain ($\hat{R} \le 1.003$, bulk effective
sample size $\ge$ 1,242, tail $\ge$ 295) and its posterior was centred close to zero
throughout, the largest estimate being −1.20 [−2.77, 0.40] years in language processing.
Leave-one-out comparison preferred the common-transition specification in all four domains,
by 0.20 to 3.06 elpd units (0.5 to 1.2 standard errors), so allowing the transition point to
differ by group buys no predictive fit; the Pareto-$\hat{k}$ diagnostics for that comparison
are themselves unreliable here ([`r sn("diagnostics")`](#note-diagnostics)). A common
transition point per domain is reported as the primary specification.

## `r sn("subtests")` — Episodic memory refitted to each sub-test {#note-subtests}

To assess whether the composite's transition and group contrast are properties of the
construct or artefacts of fixed weighting, the episodic model was refitted to each
constituent sub-test separately, z-scored on the same normative basis
(`sensitivity_3.3_subtest_refits.R`).

```{r tab-subtests, eval = file.exists("sensitivity_3.3_subtest_table.csv")}
SUBTESTS <- c(lmi_unit_tot  = "Logical Memory I (immediate recall)",
              lmii_unit_tot = "Logical Memory II (delayed recall)",
              ravlt_t15_tot = "RAVLT trials 1–5 total (verbal list learning)",
              pal_ftm_score = "CANTAB PAL first-trial memory score (paired-associate learning)")

read.csv('sensitivity_3.3_subtest_table.csv') |>
  transmute(label  = unname(SUBTESTS[subtest]),
            var    = subtest,
            N      = n_obs,
            omega  = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", omega_mean, omega_q5, omega_q95),
            ph_b1  = sprintf("%.3f", PH_b1grp),
            ph_sum = sprintf("%.3f", PH_b1grp_d1grp)) |>
  supp_gt("subtests", "Episodic memory model refitted to each sub-test",
          subtitle = sprintf(paste(
            "Intervals are 90%%. Composite estimates for comparison are in Table 2 (main text)",
            "and %s."), sn("transition"))) |>
  gt::cols_label(label  = "Sub-test", var = "Variable", N = "Observations",
                 omega  = lab("&omega; [90% CrI]", "$\\omega$ [90\\% CrI]"),
                 ph_b1  = lab("&beta;<sub>1</sub> group", "$\\beta_1$ group"),
                 ph_sum = lab("&beta;<sub>1</sub> + &delta;<sub>1</sub> group", "$\\beta_1 + \\delta_1$ group")) |>
  gt::tab_spanner("P(H)", columns = c(ph_b1, ph_sum)) |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = N) |>
  gt::cols_align("left", columns = c(label, var)) |>
  gt::cols_align("right", columns = c(omega, ph_b1, ph_sum)) |>
  mono(var) |>
  pdf_hide(var)
```

Interpretation must take account of a design feature of the battery: the four sub-tests
differ in how much retest practice effect they permit. Because the pre-transition slope
$\beta_1$ is substantially a practice effect, any instrument that suppresses practice
compresses the quantity $\beta_1$ measures is not evidence against the composite finding.

The post-transition contrast, which is least confounded with practice, replicates broadly.
It is supported in three of four sub-tests, including both practice-mitigated instruments
(verbal list learning and paired-associate learning). Since decline after the transition is
not a practice phenomenon, this is the more meaningful sub-test replication of the group
finding, and it holds where practice can't explain it.

## `r sn("attrition")` — Attrition and cognition-related dropout {#note-attrition}

Participants contributed four to seven of up to seven possible assessment waves. Dropout
related to cognitive status would bias observed trajectories optimistically: participants
who are declining, or already performing less well, are plausibly more likely to leave, so
later waves over-represent healthier survivors.

```{r tab-waves}
sessions_wilcox <- wilcox.test(Sessions ~ Group, data = demographics)

demographics |>
  mutate(Group = factor(Group, levels = c('Control', 'Experimental'),
                        labels = c('Control', 'Education'))) |>
  group_by(Group) |>
  summarise(N = n(), mean_s = mean(Sessions, na.rm = TRUE),
            median_s = median(Sessions, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') |>
  supp_gt("waves", "Assessment waves completed by group",
          subtitle = sprintf("Wilcoxon rank-sum test of waves completed between groups: p = %s.",
                             fmt_pval(sessions_wilcox$p.value, 2))) |>
  gt::cols_label(N = "Participants", mean_s = "Mean", median_s = "Median") |>
  gt::tab_spanner("Waves completed", columns = c(mean_s, median_s)) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = mean_s, decimals = 2) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = median_s, decimals = 0) |>
  gt::cols_align("left", columns = Group)
```

```{r tab-baseline-attrition}
baseline_domains <- d3 |>
  dplyr::filter(phase == 1) |>
  transmute(IDCode, Group,
            episodic, working, language,
            executive = -executive) |>  # sign-flip to match higher-is-better convention
  left_join(demographics |> select(IDCode, Sessions), by = 'IDCode') |>
  mutate(completion = if_else(Sessions >= median(Sessions, na.rm = TRUE),
                              'More waves', 'Fewer waves'))

attrition_cognition <- baseline_domains |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(episodic, working, executive, language),
               names_to = 'Domain', values_to = 'value') |>
  group_by(Domain) |>
  summarise(
    rho    = suppressWarnings(cor.test(Sessions, value, method = 'spearman')$estimate),
    p_cor  = suppressWarnings(cor.test(Sessions, value, method = 'spearman')$p.value),
    mean_more_waves  = mean(value[completion == 'More waves'],  na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_fewer_waves = mean(value[completion == 'Fewer waves'], na.rm = TRUE),
    p_ttest = t.test(value ~ completion)$p.value,
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) |>
  mutate(Domain = factor(DOMAINS[Domain], levels = DOMAINS)) |>
  arrange(Domain)

attrition_cognition |>
  mutate(p_cor = fmt_pval(p_cor), p_ttest = fmt_pval(p_ttest)) |>
  supp_gt("baseline_attrition", "Baseline cognition by number of waves completed",
          subtitle = paste("Baseline composite scores (z; higher is better in every domain).",
                           "Completion is split at the median number of waves.")) |>
  gt::cols_label(rho = lab("Spearman &rho;", "Spearman $\\rho$"), p_cor = "p",
                 mean_more_waves = "At or above median", mean_fewer_waves = "Below median",
                 p_ttest = "p (Welch t)") |>
  gt::tab_spanner("Correlation with waves completed", columns = c(rho, p_cor)) |>
  gt::tab_spanner("Mean baseline score", columns = c(mean_more_waves, mean_fewer_waves, p_ttest)) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(rho, mean_more_waves, mean_fewer_waves), decimals = 3) |>
  gt::cols_align("left", columns = Domain) |>
  gt::cols_align("right", columns = c(p_cor, p_ttest))
```

Waves completed did not differ between arms (Wilcoxon p =
`r round(sessions_wilcox$p.value, 2)`), so differential attrition between groups is not a
concern for the group contrasts specifically. Baseline episodic memory and language
processing were both associated with the number of waves completed, while working memory
and executive function were not.

### Sensitivity refit conditioning on completion {#completion-refit}

To assess how far this could account for the reported slopes, the episodic and language
models were refitted with the number of waves completed entered on both the intercept and
the pre-transition slope. If the trajectory findings were an artefact of cognition-related
dropout, conditioning on completion should attenuate them substantially.

```{r tab-attrition-refit}
tibble(
  Domain   = rep(c(DOMAINS[["episodic"]], DOMAINS[["language"]]), each = 2),
  Contrast = rep(c("β₁ group", "β₁ + δ₁ group"), 2),
  est_pri  = c(pci(m.ep, GB1, 3),   pci(m.ep, c(GB1, GD1), 3),
               pci(m.la, GB1, 3),   pci(m.la, c(GB1, GD1), 3)),
  est_adj  = c(pci(m.ep.s, GB1, 3), pci(m.ep.s, c(GB1, GD1), 3),
               pci(m.la.s, GB1, 3), pci(m.la.s, c(GB1, GD1), 3)),
  ph_pri   = c(pH(m.ep, GB1),   pH(m.ep, c(GB1, GD1)),
               pH(m.la, GB1),   pH(m.la, c(GB1, GD1))),
  ph_adj   = c(pH(m.ep.s, GB1), pH(m.ep.s, c(GB1, GD1)),
               pH(m.la.s, GB1), pH(m.la.s, c(GB1, GD1)))
) |>
  supp_gt("attrition_refit",
          "Group contrasts before and after conditioning on waves completed",
          subtitle = "Estimates are z per year, posterior mean [95% CrI]. Hypothesis: Education > Control.",
          groupname_col = "Domain") |>
  gt::cols_label(Contrast = "Contrast", est_pri = "Primary", est_adj = "Adjusted for completion",
                 ph_pri = "Primary", ph_adj = "Adjusted") |>
  gt::tab_spanner("Estimate [95% CrI]", columns = c(est_pri, est_adj)) |>
  gt::tab_spanner("P(H)", columns = c(ph_pri, ph_adj)) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(ph_pri, ph_adj), decimals = 3) |>
  gt::cols_align("left", columns = Contrast) |>
  gt::cols_align("right", columns = c(est_pri, est_adj))
```

Conditioning on completion left every contrast essentially unchanged. Had the reported group
differences been generated by cognition-related dropout, conditioning on realised completion
should have attenuated them substantially; it does not. The language post-transition
estimate is if anything slightly larger under adjustment, with a wider interval, which is
consistent with completion carrying a little of the signal but not with it producing the
effect.

## `r sn("sbc")` — Simulation-based calibration {#note-sbc}

The exact model configuration reported here — all priors as specified, $\rho$ fixed at 3,
$\sigma_u$ as specified — was validated by simulation-based calibration [Talts et al. 2020;
Modrák et al. 2025]. We took 500 replicates per configuration, using a bootstrapped real
design matrix (covariates only, no cognitive scores) so that covariate collinearity and the
group imbalance were realistic. Critically, the one-sided contrasts on which the reported
inferences rest, $\beta_{1,\text{Group}}$ and
$\beta_{1,\text{Group}} + \delta_{1,\text{Group}}$, were treated as test quantities rather
than inferred from marginal parameter calibration. This matters because the reported fits
show a posterior correlation of about $-0.9$ between the two coefficients, so the sum is
dominated by a dependence that wouldn't be detected by per-parameter rank histograms.

**Evidence-ratio calibration.** Where the model reported an effect in the hypothesized
direction with probability >0.99, it was replicated through simulation about that often.
However, almost all simulated datasets ended up in that range because the priors on the
group coefficients were wider than the effects observed, leaving too few replicates in the
moderate range to assess calibration there. Calibration in the range that working memory and
executive function occupy is therefore not established by this run.

**Rank calibration.** Every estimated parameter passed on all 500 replicates and on the
convergence-filtered subset: $\omega$, $\sigma$, $\sigma_u$, the $\beta_0$ and $\beta_1$
terms, both $\delta_1$ terms, both inferential contrasts and a joint log-likelihood
sentinel, each within a 95% simultaneous ECDF confidence band. All 500 fits were free of
divergent transitions and met the effective-sample-size criterion.
